Posted April 21, 2003
(MarijuanaNews note: There were many interesting speeches at the NORML conference, but I think that easily the most important was given by Canadian Senator Pierre Claude Nolin, who headed the committee that produced the Canadian Senate reportrecommending the legalization of cannabis.

Quite often, such reports are prepared by staffers, while the politicians who take the credit know little more than what is in the press release that accompanies it. That is definitely not the case with Senator Nolin. He really gets it.

He even went so far as to spend a couple of nights sleeping with the junkies on the streets of Vancouver's East side to see what that world is really like. This is no ordinary politician.

He also understands that Canadian cannabis legalization would be an ideological threat to DEAland prohibitionism, but not because of either Canadian cannabis going south or even American tourists going north.
See
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

Freedom anywhere is a threat to tyranny everywhere.
See
 Why the US won't let Australia reform its drug laws. The real drug war

But the proof that freedom works next door is clearly very horrifying to the ideologues in Washington.

Senator Nowlin also understands the importance of cannabis policy in dealing with the hard drug problem.
See
 Marijuana Legalization, The Missing Pillar in Solving the Substance Abuse Problem in Vancouver and All of Canada. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Freedom has a friend in Ottawa.

The article below is the latest and most bizarre manifestation of the DEAland fear of freedom on its borders, but this borders on the absurd. It will surely anger many Canadians, even those who do not really care about cannabis policies.)

Canada's pending drug law irks U.S.
Decriminalization of marijuana likely to strain relations, White House says
By Janice Tibbetts
CanWest News Service
http://www.canada.com

April 19, 2003
Justice Minister Martin Cauchon says he has not consulted his American counterparts on his plans to relax Canada's marijuana laws -- prompting a warning from a White House official that sidelining the U.S. could become another irritant in relations between the federal government and Washington.

Failure to talk to the Americans about pending marijuana laws is akin to Canada unilaterally setting up " open-air toxic waste sites " along the border, said Tom Riley, public affairs director for the White House office of drug control policy.
(MarijuanaNews note: The Bush Administration views freedom as toxic waste.)

" I think there is a bit of an analog here, " said Mr. Riley, repeating U.S. drug czar John Walters' assertion that eased drug laws will trigger tighter security checks for Canadians who cross the border.
(MarijuanaNews note: Slowing down traffic at the Canadian border hurts American businesses. At a time when tourism is hurting, this stupidity will create a backlash. Canada is also our largest energy source. And what will they say if the Canadian Supreme court says that Canadians have a right to possess cannabis.)
See
Ontario Judge Prods Canadian Government On Medical Cannabis Program. Supreme Court Hearings On All Cannabis Prohibition Now Set For May. We Are Winning!

Mr. Cauchon intends to introduce legislation late this spring to decriminalize possession of less than 30 grams of marijuana, the equivalent of about 25 cigarettes. People caught with small amounts would be punished with a fine rather than a criminal record.

Decriminalization will be yet another sore point in already fragile Canada-U.S. relations, predicted Chris Sands, a Canadian expert with the Center for International and Strategic Studies in Washington.
(MarijuanaNews note: If one wants an excellent example of how cannabis prohibition causes brain damage, this would be it. Click on Sands name to get his background. He is very well educated, and the rightwing think tank for which he works does not hire dummies. The usual job of think tanks is to enable dumb people to say something smart. This seems to reverse that process.

Also, it is odd that this story devotes so much space to an unofficial source. It would be interesting to know how this happened.)

" I know that Canadian politicians think this shouldn't be turned into such a big deal, but there is no room for persuasion down here and I think it's going to be very damaging if Canada chooses to go ahead.
(MarijuanaNews note: Twelve states have decriminalized cannabis possession, including the border states of Ohio on Lake Erie and Maine. In Ohio 100 grams, more than is being contemplated by Cauchon, is subject to a $100 fine. Roughly 70% of Americans favor decrim, but Sands says there is no room for persuasion. He has obviously confused the Bush/Ashcroft axis of hypocrisy with the American people. But so did the Supreme Court.)

" My guess is they'll decriminalize, start paying the price and then consult, which is the worst way to do things. It is better to consult before than after a tragedy. "

Mr. Cauchon said that he has not talked to the Americans about his plans, nor would he confirm whether they would be among the stakeholders who will be asked for input after he tables his bill.

" We haven't talked to the Americans so far, " he said. " We may be talking to the Americans after we have made up our mind as regard to the policy. My primary goal here -- I'm minister of justice for Canada -- is to make sure we are going to have a good policy here in Canada, for Canadians. "
This is an improvement, see
Ottawa Citizen Columnist Dan Gardner Assails Canadian Justice Minister's Kowtowing to UN and DEAland Narks: " U.S. says jump, we say how high? "
and links

But he said he wants to send a message to the U.S. that marijuana will still be illegal in Canada and that police will be instructed to be vigilant in enforcing the law.
See
Canadian Justice Minister Calls for National Debate On Cannabis Policies And Begins It By Debating Himself. Phony Decrim Bill May Be Used As Cover To Increase Penalties for Growing.

Mike Murphy, a spokesman for Mr. Cauchon, said there have been lower-level consultations among bureaucrats in the U.S. and Canada, but he would give no further details. He added that Canada should be free to make its own laws and does not intend to back down to satisfy the U.S.
(MarijuanaNews note: On Saturday morning, I did not have the time to do my usual surf and search, but I just happened to go to the National Post [one of Canada's two national news papers,] and this story was linked on its homepage. [It was also published in the Ottawa Citizen.] I told Eugene Oscapella of the Canadian Foundation for Drug Policyabout it, and he read a brief excerpt including that sentence to the conference. It brought a cheer. Our Founding Fathers would be incredulous that American freedom depends on Canadian independence!)

While Mr. Sands agreed that the U.S. should not be able to dictate Canadian law, he said that high-level consultations would be useful so that Canadian politicians could get a better picture of how " uptight " the U.S. is about softening drug laws.
See
Walters Concedes That Canada Can Legalize Cannabis If It Wants To, Which Was The Only True Thing He Said While In Montreal.

" I know most Canadians think of it as a happy, happy, hippie, free-love issue, but it's really an indictment against Canadian law enforcement that is going to be hard to shake if you go forward with it, " Mr. Sands said.
(MarijuanaNews note: An expert on Canada at a Washington think tank says that if Canada follows the 25 year-old example of Ohio, Maine, California, et al., it will be an indictment against Canadian law enforcement. "??)

" Any consultation that helps drill that in with Canadian government officials is helpful. "

The U.S. is particularly concerned because of the growing presence of potent B.C. bud, which landed Canada for the first time this year on a list of drug countries that U.S. President George W. Bush sent to Congress in January.
(MarijuanaNews note: Has potent B.C. bud become one word, like sophisticated hydroponic grow op. "?

According to the US Department of Justice web site, Marijuana produced in Canada is recognized for its potency, but there is a general misconception regarding the uniqueness of this marijuana. Growers in both Canada and the United States have access to the same strains of cannabis seeds and the same cultivation technologies. Therefore, growers in both countries are capable of producing the same quality of high-grade marijuana.

Moreover, Canada provides perhaps two percent of the DEAland cannabis supply, at most.)
See
Is The War On Cannabis A Cult? Taking Cannabiphobia To New Depths Of Absurdity. A Method to Their Madness?

" I think a lot of eyebrows were raised about Canada being on a list with Columbia and Guatemala and Mexico and Haiti and countries like that, " said Mr. Riley.

Mr. Sands had grim predictions for how U.S. law enforcement officials will treat Canadians after Canada softens its drug laws.

" What I think will probably start happening is they'll demand a list of everybody who is not arrested for marijuana possession but is found in possession of marijuana by the cops and they'll want to have that as part of the record when your passport is scanned, " he said.

" There will be another whole category of Canadians who have diminished access to the United States. "
(MarijuanaNews note: We couldn't make this up. The prohibitionists want Canadian police to give names of Canadians who are ticketed for possession to DEAland so that they can be barred from the land of the drug-free. And this would not be a new category.
From 1998 see
It Is Now Official Policy For Employees Of The Royal Ontario Museum To Lie To US Customs Officials.

Now do you understand why I call it DEAland?)
